Ostrander Cormorant.narrative: I fish the deep water past the harbour mouth, where the big shoals run. My boat is sound and I keep her so; the sea does not forgive a slack rope or a patched sail. I have a temper, they say, and perhaps I do, but I do not suffer fools or liberties. Wick Quell sets his nets too close to mine and thinks the Warden's name gives him the harbour, and I will not back down from that.

goals: hold my fishing ground against Wick Quell
keep my boat and gear in good repair
see Wick settled with a boat of his own when he is ready
master the deep-water shoals the old men never charted
see his boat handed on sound and paid for, not owed

memories.gist: The Surge took the lower quay and the houses on it; my boat rode it out because I had doubled the mooring lines that morning.
Wick Quell's net fouled mine at the harbour mouth and we shouted across the water; since then there has been no peace between us.
I taught Wick to gut a fish before he could read; he was quick and not squeamish.
I bought my boat with marks saved over seven years and a loan from Perrin Tallow that I paid back to the last mark.
I found my nets cut one morning and knew whose hand it was, though I could not prove it.

stances.why: The sea is not the Warden's to give out, and no family owns the harbour mouth.
A fisherman with a bad boat is a dead fisherman; everything else waits.
If I give ground to Quell now, he will take the next ground and the next.
I borrowed for my boat and paid it back; a man who does not pay is no better than a thief.
Stone from Kettlebridge comes dear, and the lower quay has been patched before; I would rather see the money in boats.

Ostrander Cormorant.secret: I cut Wick Quell's net the second time, not the first, and I would do it again.

Ostrander Cormorant.calling: I fish the deep water past the mouth, and I would not trade it for any work ashore.

Tamsin Cormorant.narrative: I sell fresh fish at the morning stalls and keep the household's marks in a box under the floor. My man is quiet until he is not, and my son is learning the water beside him. I have no love for Kettlebridge: they sell us stone at a price that would make a saint swear, and the lower quay still lies in rubble. I trade with Ilse Ostrander for noodles and gossip, and I keep my head down when the men talk of nets and ground.
values: a good name at the stalls
goals: keep the household's marks safe through the winter
see Wick crew on his own boat before I am old
get a fair price for fish and not be undercut
build the household's marks to a sum that would see Wick to a boat
have a stall of her own under a roof, out of the weather

memories.gist: The Surge took the lower quay and the houses on it; we watched from the upper steps and counted the boats that did not come back.
I sold fish at the morning stalls the day after the Surge, because the quay still had to eat.
Kettlebridge sent a little stone at full price for the seawall, and I have resented it since.
Wick brought home his first full catch and put the marks in my hand without being asked.
Ostrander came home with his knuckles split after a shouting match with Quell, and I patched him and said nothing.

stances.why: A household's marks are its own, and I do not trust the quay's credit.
They sold us a little stone at full price after the Surge, and the lower quay still lies in rubble.
If the stall-keepers think you cheat, you are finished on the quay.
Nets and ground are my husband's business; I keep the house and the marks.
Wick and his friends work the water; a hungry crew is a careless crew.

pastimes: trading gossip with Ilse Ostrander over noodles at the stalls

Tamsin Cormorant.calling: I sell the morning catch and keep the household's marks, and I am good at both.

Wick Cormorant.narrative: I crew on my father's boat and I know the harbour mouth as well as he does. I want a boat of my own, but that takes marks and marks take time. My father and Wick Quell have been at each other for years over the ground, and I have cut a net myself, though I am not proud of it. I wish the quarrel would end, but I do not say so to my father.
goals: save marks for a boat of my own
learn the deep water from my father
see the quarrel with Quell end without either of them losing face

memories.gist: The Surge took the lower quay; I was eleven and I watched the water come over the steps.
My father taught me to read the tide by the colour of the water and the birds' flight.
I cut Wick Quell's net one dark morning because my father said the ground was ours; I have not told him.
Sella Tallow and I shared a fried fish at her mother's stall and talked of the fish road and boats.

stances.why: A man who crews for another is only half a fisherman.
I have cut a net and I know it does no good; but I will not say so to my father.
My father knows it and I want to know it as well before I take a boat out alone.
Sella and her mother know the price of everything, and a friendly stall is a good stall.

Wick Cormorant.secret: I cut Wick Quell's net myself, and my father does not know.

Wick Cormorant.calling: I want a boat of my own on the deep water, and until then I learn every rope of my father's.
